test_title: PYST 6: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The offer had not been expected to be withdrawn at the last moment.

options.text: Someone had not expected the offer to be withdrawn at the last moment.
The withdrawal of the offer was not expected.
Nobody expected that the offer withdrew.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the passive voice: "The offer had not been expected to be withdrawn at the last moment."
 
• The main verb is in the **Past Perfect Tense** (had been + V3).
 
• Since the agent (the person doing the expecting) is not mentioned in the passive sentence, we use a vague pronoun like "Someone" or "They" as the subject in the active voice.
 
• To convert to active voice: 
 
 
• The dummy subject "Someone" is introduced.
 
• The passive verb "had not been expected" changes to the active form "had not expected."
 
• The original subject "the offer" becomes the direct object.
 
• The infinitive phrase "to be withdrawn at the last moment" remains to complete the meaning.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Someone had not expected the offer to be withdrawn at the last moment."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The withdrawal of the offer was not expected." – This uses a noun phrase ("The withdrawal") and remains in a passive-style structure with the simple past "was."
 
• **Option 3: **"The offer withdrew itself unexpectedly." – This changes the meaning; an offer cannot perform the action of withdrawing itself, and it omits the "expecting" part of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"Nobody expected that the offer withdrew." – This changes the tense to Simple Past and incorrectly uses "withdrew" (active) instead of the required passive sense for the offer's status.
